'''Carpetbag steak''' is a uniquely Australian dish that was first popularised in Sydney around 1950. 

==Ingredients ==
* 1 Scotch [[Cookbook:Steak|fillet steak]] (thickly-cut)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] (optional)
* Ground [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|black pepper]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|Cayenne pepper]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|Lemon juice]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]] (optional)
* 3–4 [[cookbook:Oyster|oyster]]s
* [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire sauce]]
* [[Cookbook:Lime|Limes]] (optional)
* Shredded [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]] (optional)

==Procedure==
#Cut a small pocket, approximately 6 cm (2.5 inches) in length and about the same depth, in the edge of the thick steak.
#If desired, season the inside of the pocket with some of salt, pepper, cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and olive oil.
#Dip the oysters into the Worcestershire sauce, and then insert them in the pocket in the steak.
#If desired, add lime pulp or some shredded cheese into the pocket.
#Seal the pocket with a moistened [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewer]].
#[[Cookbook:Barbecuing|Barbecue]], [[Cookbook:Grilling|grill]], or [[Cookbook:Broiling|broil]] the steak to your desired level of [[Cookbook:Meat and Poultry#Doneness|doneness]]. Alternatively, cook over a moderate heat in a heavy-based [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]].

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Substitutes for Worcestershire sauce include [[Cookbook:Teriyaki Sauce|teriyaki sauce]], [[Cookbook:Oyster sauce|oyster sauce]] or red wine vinegar marinades, or the steak has the marinade or sauce.
*Substitutes for oysters include [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]], [[Cookbook:Crawfish|yabbies]], and [[Cookbook:Shrimp|prawns]].
*Some recipes [[Cookbook:Poaching|poach]] or [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] the oysters first a little, if the diners prefer rare steak but not raw oysters.
*Some recipes wrap the steak in [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]] or [[Cookbook:Pancetta|pancetta]].
*If applicable and desired, you can [[Cookbook:Deglazing|deglaze]] the cooking pan with [[Cookbook:Sherry|sherry]] or [[Cookbook:Brandy|brandy]], or make a reduction of oyster liquid and [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]] with chopped [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]].
